body:
CORRECTION: MY BUG-1522 + BUG-1525 PAIRING WAS WRONG. I verified the reviewer's
three refutations myself rather than just accepting them, and all three hold.

  1. NO FORKED LINEAGE. There is no bare bug-1460 branch anywhere -- only
     bug-1460-work locally, on origin and on gitlab. BUG-1525 never fired here.
  2. THE DRAIN NEVER READS BRIEFS. The single occurrence of "brief" in
     auto_complete.rs is the word inside a doc comment at line 1417. There is no
     brief-reading in the phase driver at all, so a drain-launched implementer
     never sees the Setup block. BUG-1525 is a HAND-DISPATCH hazard.
  3. MY THIRD ROUND WAS NOT SILENT. Commit 2cb2c15c42, "test(drain): harden CI
     ordering regression (BUG-1460)", is committed 2026-09-20T21:42:38-07:00 =
     04:42:38Z -- thirty-four seconds BEFORE the 04:43:12Z PhaseDonePr I counted
     as a third no-op. That round produced work.

So the evidence is TWO silent rounds then a successful one, not three in a row.
That is not a cosmetic difference: three-in-a-row reads as a systematic loop,
two-then-success reads as a condition that CLEARED -- and only the second
reading points at the cause. The reviewer's candidate is BUG-1524, a diverged
local -work branch making phase 1 refuse, the drain treating the refusal as
recoverable and continuing from the CI gate onto the previous round's green.
That fits the two silent rounds exactly and I have no competing account.

WHAT SURVIVES FROM MY SIDE, unchanged: BUG-1522 is real and independently
verifiable -- rework_no_op_failure is consulted only in the PrOpened arm at
auto_complete.rs:3689, while the ~3623, 3681 (Punted/Proceed) and 3717
(AlreadyMerged) arms advance without it. That is why the refusal in 1 was not
caught. It is the detector, and it is now paired with BUG-1524 rather than
BUG-1525.

REVISED FIX ORDER:
  BUG-1524  the cause of the silent rounds
  BUG-1485  the misattribution, five occurrences
  BUG-1522  the detector
  BUG-1525  still real, still worth fixing, but its blast radius is the BRIEF
            lane -- which matters because the BUG-1470 brief is about to travel
            exactly that path.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the shape is worth more than the conclusion. I had
solid evidence for the guard being unreachable and then grafted a CAUSE onto it
that I never checked. I did not run `git ls-remote origin bug-1460`. One command
would have falsified the pairing before I sent it to two seats.

And I counted three silent rounds from three PhaseDonePr events without checking
whether commits landed between them -- which is the filter-presented-as-finding
pattern I named in the very same message, two paragraphs after committing it.
Counting events is not the same as counting rounds, exactly as counting a streak
is not the same as measuring a rate.

The reviewer's check was the cheap one and mine was the expensive one. I should
have tried to falsify the pairing before broadcasting it, not after.
subject: CORRECTION: my BUG-1522+BUG-1525 pairing was wrong — verified; the pair is BUG-1524+BUG-1522 and there were two silent rounds, not three
